“That will not be enough,” said Tom, and looked at Robert. Jack searched for the key for a long time at the harbour, without success. Whoever found the barrel, said Jack, was to tell Tom. Someone had closed the shutters without giving a reason. The lamplight trembled as someone opened the door. “Say nothing more,” said Tom. “That will not be enough,” Robert replied.

The fire crackled in the stove, and the shadows wandered across the wall. For a while nobody said anything, and that was worse than any word. In the stable, it was said, Emma had last seen the sack of salt. Robert searched for the crate for a long time up on the pass, without success. Robert did not answer. Alice put the lantern down under the bridge and waited. Tom arrived under the bridge when Jack had already left. Tom searched for the book for a long time up on the pass, without success. Far below in the valley a bell struck, then again, then no more. The dog raised its head as if it had heard something, and laid it down again. Jack put the rope down behind the wall and waited.
The next day Mary set off with the sack of salt under one arm, without saying goodbye. The lamplight trembled as someone opened the door. It was a grey noon, and behind the wall nothing stirred.
